correctness.rationale: With F(z)=(z^n−a)(z^n−b), F′(z)=conj(z)F(z) gives a quadratic in w=z^n whose discriminant is (a−b)²t(t−2n)+n²(a+b)²>0 for t>0, hence w real (including t=2n). At positive rays angular log-H curvature is positive and cannot yield local maxima; on negative rays it is strictly negative. Radial stationarity is P(u)=u^{2n}−2nu^{2n−2}+(a+b)u^n−n(a+b)u^{n−2}+ab, with four alternating Descartes signs; the radial derivative starts and ends negative, giving at most two maxima on each of n negative rays, plus origin. Exact n=11 rational sign sequence (−,+,−,+,−) for a=50000,b=4800000 yields four simple roots, hence 23 nondegenerate maxima. For every n≥12, at a=0 the B_n curve has two distinct turns (discriminant n²−12n+4>0), and perturbing small positive a produces four simple stationary roots and open saturation. Finite independently computed n=11/12 signs corroborate, while analytic proof covers all n≥3.
